applicability.scope: Bounded monolithic multimodal_gen composed-pipeline state and lifecycle diagnosis; actual backend/model behavior requires native validation.
applicability.prerequisites: Pinned source or a concrete trace of the selected composed-pipeline executor and installed residency manager, with the applicable monolithic route identified.
applicability.input_contract: Source/build, backend and executor/pipeline class, model revision, modality/shape, steps/scheduler/seed/output count, grouped/serial route, ranks, placement, warmup/save settings and symptom; timeout cases need correlated request/job and client/scheduler/worker events.
applicability.produced_artifact: A version-bound owner/event ledger, first unresolved boundary, causal hypothesis, smallest real discriminating check, exact results and missing dependencies.
applicability.failure_modes: Assuming all executors share the SyncExecutor contract, treating closed component use as eviction, assuming grouped schedulers are isolated, or reading socket close/job deletion as stopped device compute can misdiagnose ownership.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop performance claims when the executing path, cleanup or output quality is unresolved; retain the failure and a known baseline rather than inferring a blanket leak or safety conclusion.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; upstream runtime and efficacy validation not run.
Supplier verified one selected source blob, not the whole archive tree.
No automatic grouped isolation, device cancellation, cross-rank recovery or performance claim.
recommendations: Trace the actual executor and separate request, stage, component-use, module, scheduler, finalizer and allocator-cache lifetimes.
Check scheduler aliases and declared output-copy policies before introducing overlap; compare real serial/grouped outputs with fixed timesteps and seeds.
Correlate worker, finalizer and device completion after client timeout or deletion; preserve an unknown execution outcome until that evidence exists.
